papers.title: HAVANA: A Hierarchical Video-Action Model for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires long-horizon instruction-consistent planning and short-horizon local planning in current geometry. Video-action models (VAMs) offer a promising way to learn predictive representations for navigation. However, existing VAMs jointly predict visual futures and local trajectories in a single process, even though they operate at different paces: future prediction remains stable across multiple updates while local trajectories must react to fresh observations. To bridge this gap, we introduce HAVANA, a dual-system VAM that decouples predictive reasoning from reactive local planning. A slow system produces a compact language-conditioned latent plan from observation history, while a fast system combines the latest plan with the current observation to generate local trajectories. Their asynchronous execution enables rapid adaptation without repeated future prediction, and no future video is generated during inference. Experiments on OmniNavBench demonstrate state-of-the-art navigation performance over prior baselines, while real-world deployments further show robust generalization to unseen environments across different robot embodiments. Our code and checkpoints will be available at this https URL .

papers.title: IMPULSE: Push First, Then Predict in V-JEPA 2 Feature Space
papers.abstract: Latent world models such as V-JEPA 2 forecast in the feature space of a video encoder, but one look at an object does not reveal how hard it is to rotate, how much it bounces or how much it slides. People find out by trying: a few pokes reveal how an object responds. IMPULSE, named after the impulse response it infers, gives a predictor in frozen V-JEPA 2 feature space the same ability. A Bayesian contact memory summarizes three short calibration pushes, a predicted object pose carries it into the predictor, and a lightweight random-Fourier pose head lets the predictor use the pose. On 512 fresh objects, in a pre-specified held-out confirmation with models sealed before the data existed, the memory lowers the 1-second feature-forecast error by 11.6-12.8% relative to the same predictor without experience, for all 8 training seeds, with a 95% seed-and-object interval excluding zero. The gain also holds for 128 objects with out-of-range physics (11.7-14.0%), and the full extension beats a plain predictor by 15.5-16.6%. An information-ladder argument, exact for ideal predictors, shows that physics reaches the features only through motion, so we measure how much the pathway lets pose help. On fresh objects, the Fourier head roughly triples the gain of a perfect memory over plain pose tokens (2.8-3.2x). Raw push measurements fed through the same pathway give a similar gain, so the Bayesian summary is not required; it condenses the trials into eight interpretable numbers. The gain is absent at contact onset and grows afterwards.

papers.title: Fast Construction of Inner Sphere Trees Using Machine Learning
papers.abstract: Collision detection for complex non-convex objects is a bottleneck in physics simulation, virtual reality, and robotics. Inner sphere trees (ISTs) answer proximity and penetration queries efficiently, but their greedy leaf-sphere construction is sequential and computationally expensive, which limits both large-scale preprocessing and runtime use. In this work, we present ML-IST, a machine-learning-based method that reformulates leaf-sphere generation as a single-shot set-prediction problem: a network predicts a fixed set of inscribed sphere candidates from multichannel voxel geometry, differentiable coverage feedback corrects the coarse prediction and fills residual gaps at finer scales, and a lightweight geometric projection enforces validity. Averaged over the test set, a single-GPU implementation of ML-IST reduces mean leaf-generation time by a factor of $2.0$--$2.6$ over single-core CPU construction across target capacities of 64--512 spheres, and qualitative results on complex models show multiscale sphere distributions that follow principal volumes and slender features. We further integrate ML-IST into the Jolt Physics and Bullet engines; in an alpha-puzzle benchmark it reaches 55.89~FPS, the highest among the compared representations (conventional IST, GImpact, and convex decomposition). These results support learned leaf generation as a practical component for fast, runtime construction of detailed collision representations.

papers.title: EgoVine: Post-Training with Branching Experience Compiled from Real-World Videos
papers.abstract: Real-world egocentric videos capture multi-step household procedures, but their recorded trajectories leave alternative actions and recovery from the learner's own mistakes largely unexplored. We introduce EgoVine, a post-training framework that turns a fixed demonstration set into interactive experience for long-horizon planning. EgoVine operates in executable symbolic environments compiled from real-world video annotations, where an agent must coordinate object manipulations under partial observation and account for delayed consequences. Restoring a decision state allows the learner to explore alternative actions and compare their eventual outcomes. Union jointly trains action generation and consequence prediction in one model, using the same executions to supervise candidate comparison and recovery. Verified repairs add recovery targets from failed attempts, while comparisons among sampled continuations guide policy updates. The updated planner then returns to the environments, with its own decisions and mistakes shaping the next round of experience. On a shared benchmark, EgoVine-1.5B achieves 81.8% success on Main planning tasks and 66.7% on longer task compositions, outperforming all evaluated Flash LLM baselines on both. EgoVine connects real demonstrations to an iterative learning process that trains compact planners on choices and futures beyond the recorded trajectories.

papers.title: Transmission Error Compensation for Industrial Robots Using Fourier Series
papers.abstract: Due to their low accuracy, industrial robots commonly require online teaching after the offline development of a robot program in simulation. The accuracy is limited by compliance and transmission errors in the robot joints. Transmission errors are defined as errors between the load-side angles of the gearboxes and the motor encoder angles. An approach to identify the transmission errors based on laser tracker measurements is presented. The developed velocity-dependent Fourier series model is integrated in a virtual commissioning software as a co-simulated functional mock-up unit. Additionally, it is used to compensate the transmission errors by correcting the setpoint from the computerized numerical control (CNC). The model identification and the compensation are experimentally evaluated with a Stäubli TX2-40 industrial robot. The model has a mean absolute error of 0.114 mrad, and the compensation improves the accuracy by 83.26 % for axis 2 and 49.21 % for axis 3.

papers.title: Lubricant Temperature Observer for Gearboxes in Industrial Robots
papers.abstract: The position and path accuracy of industrial robots is strongly affected by temperature. In particular, temperature-dependent friction and altered hysteresis and transmission errors in the gearboxes are the main causes of these deviations. Since standard industrial robots lack temperature sensors, it is proposed to estimate the gearbox lubricant temperature using observer structures. It is planned to apply the proposed lubricant temperature observer to provide the input for temperature-dependent error compensation for gearboxes in industrial robots. First, a two-state heat transfer model describing the heat transfer from the lubricant through the gearbox housing to the environment is described and identified. It is integrated into a Luenberger observer and a Kalman filter with a correction of the lubricant temperature estimation based on measurements from a housing temperature sensor. Temperature measurements were performed in an experimental setup with a cycloidal gear filled with grease, which is common for industrial robots. Due to its changing viscosity and changing thermal conductivity at different shear rates, it shows a less uniform thermal behavior than gear-oil. For the validation measurements, the developed observers showed a mean absolute error of 1.3 K.

executive_summary: Planning and computation: FLASH-CBF-RRT reportedly matched RRT-Connect's 100% success across 689 MotionBenchMaker problems while reducing median planning time by 3.82x. CusADi2 reportedly lowered GPU evaluation latency versus all tested baselines at batch sizes of 64 to 4096, but only matched them at larger batch sizes.

Long-horizon manipulation: DreamCan reports 91.2% success on LIBERO-Long using sparse subgoals from action-free videos and a 0.1B-parameter low-level policy, plus real-world bimanual demonstrations. FIBER reports 42.0% mean simulation success across 128 variations per task, versus 11.6% for projected latent replay and 3.5% for kinematic planning; its hardware evidence consists of demonstrations.

Hardware demonstrations show distinct capabilities, with different evaluation scopes: a quadruped completed three autonomous Rubik's Cube solves using only its feet, each taking about 30 steps over 8-9 minutes. CLARO reports 88.8% robot-arm retrieval success in clutter, while DexOAK reports 46/56 successful open-loop hardware replays across five tasks.

Adaptation and deployment: PIA reports reliable few-shot autonomous-racing adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction. ChairNav reports increasing mean distance between user interventions from 29.2 m to 57.4 m after post-training and autonomous operation for 93.4% of total driving time on kilometer-scale urban sidewalk routes.

Evaluation exposes important limitations: on six ContactBench tasks, evaluated vision-only policies struggled with contact events, and visual-tactile policies did not meaningfully improve performance. ForagerSim's learned policies fell short of humans in larger or topologically complex environments under simplified 2D sensing. ACTS showed contact-consistent tactile predictions in inspected robot rollouts, but mixed visual transfer, sometimes worse than frame copying.

Workforce implications remain conditional: the robotics-exposure study reports higher exposure in physically intensive occupations and those with lower wages and education requirements. Its authors explicitly characterize these measures as an upper bound on potential exposure—not evidence of deployment readiness, cost competitiveness, or adoption.

institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce FLASH-CBF-RRT, using closed-form collision-clearance bounds to choose how long a CBF-filtered velocity can remain constant. Across 689 MotionBenchMaker problems, the authors report matching RRT-Connect's 100% success rate while reducing median planning time by 3.82x; they also report being 3.88x faster than fixed-step CBF-RRT. On a 17-DoF mobile manipulator, the authors report 2.2x faster planning and 4.2x fewer evaluations.

institution_matches.title: Solving a Giant Rubik's Cube with a Quadruped Robot
institution_matches.overview: The authors combine onboard RGB-D perception and planning with reinforcement-learned whole-body skills distilled into policies using onboard depth and proprioception. institution_matches.title: Action-Aligned Latent Planning for Versatile Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: The authors propose FIBER, projecting task-specific policies into a frozen behavioral foundation model's executable latent space and training a unified perceptive planner offline. institution_matches.title: Vector-Quantized World Model: Latent Feedback Motion Planning for Robot Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce VQ-WM, combining discrete latent search with continuous visual feedback control and using estimated first-passage time to align the latent abstraction with controller capabilities. For physical-robot Tower of Hanoi manipulation, the authors report 100\% success using only short-play data, contrasting with evaluated foundation models that succeed only when the solution trace is in their training dataset. institution_matches.title: Long-Horizon Multi-Object Rearrangement via Distilled Tree Search over Continuous Actions
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce DISCO, which uses progressive-widening MCTS in physics simulation and periodically distills search-generated plans into a policy-value model deployable without simulator-based search. institution_matches.title: Policy Search in Code Space for Multi-Agent Pathfinding
institution_matches.overview: The authors study human-directed policy search in code space, with coding agents refining algorithms through simulation feedback and correctness verification. On a challenging competition map, the authors report that a two-day search found a policy exceeding the stronger locally reproduced competition entry by 35.0% on the densest instance, with generalization to unseen map instances. In simulated warehouses, the authors report 58.9% higher throughput than a calibrated proprietary solution; under stated assumptions, they also prove collision freedom and finite-time completion of accepted goals that are not withdrawn or replaced.

institution_matches.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce PIA, pretraining a world model on heterogeneous simulated trajectories and adapting it with limited target-domain interaction through uncertainty-regularized planning. In autonomous-racing simulation, the authors report faster adaptation across track and surface shifts than strong baselines, with lower lap times and fewer failures. evidence.evidence_quote: On hardware, PIA achieves reliable few-shot adaptation with less than one hour of on-vehicle interaction.

institution_matches.title: DexOAK: Object-Aware Kinematic Retargeting
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce DexOAK, learning object-aware hand retargeting from graph-based seed references and refining the network with contact, non-penetration, and self-collision losses. On the Inspire hand, the authors report success improving from 39.5% to 48.4% on OakInk-v2 and ADD-AUC improving from 62.7% to 77.9% on ARCTIC. institution_matches.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
institution_matches.overview: The authors propose CoopUQ, combining cross-robot occupancy forecasting with constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning that penalizes predicted occupied or highly uncertain regions. institution_matches.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce Ropedia W0, a cross-embodiment egocentric loco-manipulation world model using camera poses for locomotion and projected skeletons for manipulation. The authors report state-of-the-art performance across five named cross-embodiment benchmarks and held-out human egocentric video, covering zero-shot inference through few-shot and full-data post-training. evidence.claim: After distillation, the authors report real-time, minute-long rollouts supporting live VR interaction.

institution_matches.title: GOFusion: Real-Time Gaussian-Occupancy Submap Fusion for Fisher-Informed Autonomous Robot Navigation
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce GOFusion, which anchors Gaussian primitives to occupancy maps and uses an online Fisher approximation to guide pruning and next-best-view planning. institution_matches.title: SWAP: Test-Time Steerable Humanoid Whole-Body Collision Avoidance
institution_matches.overview: The authors propose a hierarchical framework combining diffusion-based motion proposals with a whole-body RL controller for tracking and balance. The authors report reliable static and dynamic obstacle avoidance in simulation and on a real Unitree G1, with test-time steering improving targeted rewards by 34% on average while maintaining a high collision avoidance rate.

institution_matches.title: ForagerSim: Evaluating Embodied Map-Based Reasoning in Large-Scale Dynamic Worlds
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce ForagerSim, a simulation platform for embodied map-based reasoning, and compare RL baselines, an engineered robotics stack, and a human player on 8 example worlds. The authors report that with simplified 2D sensing, learned policies handle search and well-alternation in simple topologies but fall short of humans in larger or topologically more complex environments, where map-based baselines perform well.

institution_matches.title: ContactBench 1.0: A Benchmark for Everyday Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce ContactBench 1.0, a contact-rich manipulation benchmark with 36 reference tasks and more than 40 object assets. On six benchmark tasks, the authors report that the evaluated vision-only policies struggle with contact events and the evaluated visual-tactile policies do not meaningfully improve performance.

institution_matches.title: Dream What I Can: Sparse Visual Planning for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce DreamCan, a hierarchical policy using sparse visual subgoals selected by dynamic programming from offline, action-free robot videos without manual annotations. institution_matches.title: SteerAct: Unlocking Action Models through Few-Shot Temporal Steering
institution_matches.institution: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Stanford University

institution_matches.title: Physical Words: A Vocabulary for Structuring Latent Reasoning in Robot Manipulation
institution_matches.overview: The authors introduce PhysWord, aligning predicted atomic action words' contextual hidden states with latent targets from future observations. institution_matches.title: CusADi2: Latency-Optimized Batch Computation of Robot Kinematics, Jacobians, and Hessians on the GPU

institution_matches.title: SSIO: Self-Supervised Inertial Odometry
institution_matches.institution: Carnegie Mellon University; Stanford University; UC Berkeley

institution_matches.title: CLARO: Clutter Aware Robot Orchestrator for Open-Vocabulary Grasping using VLM Agents

institution_matches.title: Vision as Proprioception: Estimating Humanoid Robot Pose from Video

institution_matches.title: ACTS: Learning Visuo-Tactile World Models from Human Physical Interaction

institution_matches.title: MOMO: Human Motion from Moving Sounds

institution_matches.title: VaDar: Implicit Goal Conditioning via Value Disaggregation

institution_matches.title: How exposed is work to robotics? Occupational, industry, and geographic measures

topic_matches.title: Learning Whole-Body Kinetic Coordination for Wheeled-Quadruped Long-Range Throwing
topic_matches.institution: Harbin Institute of Technology; Tsinghua University; Zhejiang University
topic_matches.overview: The authors combine kinetic-chain arm modeling, SQP-based trajectory optimization, and reference-guided reinforcement learning for coordinated wheeled-quadruped throwing. The authors report that enabling whole-body coordination increases release speed to 16.64 m/s and throwing distance to 28.25 m. The authors report hardware validation of the complete policy across flat ground, grass, slopes, and rough roads.

evidence.claim: The authors combine kinetic-chain arm modeling, SQP-based trajectory optimization, and reference-guided reinforcement learning for coordinated wheeled-quadruped throwing.
evidence.evidence_quote: combines kinetic-chain arm modeling with SQP-based trajectory optimization and a reference-guided reinforcement learning policy for coordinated base motion

evidence.claim: The authors report that enabling whole-body coordination increases release speed to 16.64 m/s and throwing distance to 28.25 m.
evidence.evidence_quote: When whole-body coordination is enabled, the system further increases the release speed to 16.64 m/s and the throwing distance to 28.25 m.

evidence.claim: The authors report hardware validation of the complete policy across flat ground, grass, slopes, and rough roads.
evidence.evidence_quote: validate the complete policy through hardware experiments on flat ground, grass, slopes, and rough roads

topic_matches.title: MoDex: Towards Universal Multi-Object Dexterous Grasping
topic_matches.overview: The authors introduce MoDex, learning residual trajectory corrections and using single-shot grasping for proximal objects versus sequential interaction for separated objects. The authors report outperforming baselines in proximal configurations, with 61.24% success on unseen objects. The authors report zero-shot sim-to-real deployment using a vision policy trained solely in simulation.

evidence.claim: The authors introduce MoDex, learning residual trajectory corrections and using single-shot grasping for proximal objects versus sequential interaction for separated objects.
evidence.evidence_quote: introducing a spatially adaptive dual-strategy that performs single-shot grasping for proximal objects and sequential interaction for separated objects

evidence.claim: The authors report outperforming baselines in proximal configurations, with 61.24% success on unseen objects.
evidence.evidence_quote: MoDex significantly outperforms baselines in proximal configurations, achieving 61.24% success on unseen objects

evidence.claim: The authors report zero-shot sim-to-real deployment using a vision policy trained solely in simulation.
evidence.evidence_quote: zero-shot sim-to-real deployment through a vision-based policy trained solely on simulation data

topic_matches.title: Language-Forcing: Advancing Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Semantic Alignment of Whole-Body World Action Models
topic_matches.overview: The authors introduce LANGUAGE-FORCING, aligning language descriptions with action-conditioned future-visual features during training, without additional inference overhead. On HumanoidArena, the authors report 79.17% average success, exceeding the strongest competing policy by 9.46 percentage points. Across five real-world tasks, the authors report average success increasing from 53.33% to 71.33% relative to the same WAM without language alignment.

evidence.claim: The authors introduce LANGUAGE-FORCING, aligning language descriptions with action-conditioned future-visual features during training, without additional inference overhead.
evidence.evidence_quote: All auxiliary components are used only during training, introducing no additional inference overhead.

evidence.claim: On HumanoidArena, the authors report 79.17% average success, exceeding the strongest competing policy by 9.46 percentage points.
evidence.evidence_quote: On HumanoidArena, LANGUAGE-FORCING achieves an average success rate of 79.17%, exceeding the strongest competing policy by 9.46 percentage points

evidence.claim: Across five real-world tasks, the authors report average success increasing from 53.33% to 71.33% relative to the same WAM without language alignment.
evidence.evidence_quote: Across five real-world tasks, language alignment raises average success from 53.33% to 71.33% over the same WAM baseline.

topic_matches.title: ESCAPE: Egocentric Sensing for Collision Avoidance and Policy Execution
topic_matches.overview: The authors introduce ESCAPE, using distributed depth measurements represented as an obstacle-aware point cloud for flow-matching-based trajectory generation. The authors report zero-shot transfer from simulation training to physical hardware without real-world fine-tuning. The authors report outperforming external-view and voxelized-planning baselines in both simulation and real-world evaluations using only egocentric perception.

evidence.claim: The authors introduce ESCAPE, using distributed depth measurements represented as an obstacle-aware point cloud for flow-matching-based trajectory generation.
evidence.evidence_quote: ESCAPE aggregates sparse measurements from distributed depth sensors, converting them into a structured, obstacle-aware point cloud representation.

evidence.claim: The authors report zero-shot transfer from simulation training to physical hardware without real-world fine-tuning.
evidence.evidence_quote: ESCAPE is trained entirely in simulation and transfers zero-shot to physical hardware without any real-world fine-tuning.

evidence.claim: The authors report outperforming external-view and voxelized-planning baselines in both simulation and real-world evaluations using only egocentric perception.
evidence.evidence_quote: outperforming external-view and voxelized-planning baselines across both simulation and real-world evaluations

topic_matches.title: Weakly Supervised Discovery of Motion Styles for Compositional Robot Control
topic_matches.overview: The authors present CODES, combining motion retargeting, weakly supervised style discovery, and reinforcement learning to compose motion styles with independent commands. In evaluations on a Unitree Go2 across two simulators and physical hardware, the authors report improved kinematic coherence relative to baselines. The authors report velocity-command tracking beyond the recorded data's support, with distinguishable styles in cross-simulator and hardware deployments.

evidence.claim: The authors present CODES, combining motion retargeting, weakly supervised style discovery, and reinforcement learning to compose motion styles with independent commands.
evidence.evidence_quote: weakly supervised consensus encoding and density-based clustering identify styles within and across recordings without a prescribed count; finally, reinforcement learning trains a policy to compose the discovered styles with independent commands.

evidence.claim: In evaluations on a Unitree Go2 across two simulators and physical hardware, the authors report improved kinematic coherence relative to baselines.
evidence.evidence_quote: We evaluate CODES on a Unitree Go2 quadruped across two simulators and physical hardware. Compared to baselines, CODES significantly improves kinematic coherence.

evidence.claim: The authors report velocity-command tracking beyond the recorded data's support, with distinguishable styles in cross-simulator and hardware deployments.
evidence.evidence_quote: our controller successfully tracks velocity commands that generalize beyond the support of the recorded data, exhibiting robust and distinguishable style characteristics during both cross-simulator and real-world hardware deployments.

topic_matches.title: ChairNav: Cross-Embodiment Pre-training and Personalization for Long-Horizon Wheelchair Navigation
topic_matches.overview: The authors present ChairNav, adapting a visual navigation model through cross-embodiment pre-training, wheelchair-demonstration mid-training, and personalization from user interventions. The authors report that pre-training reduces lateral ADE by 18%, while post-training increases mean distance between user interventions from 29.2 m to 57.4 m. On kilometer-scale urban sidewalk routes, the authors report autonomous operation for 93.4% of total driving time.

evidence.claim: The authors present ChairNav, adapting a visual navigation model through cross-embodiment pre-training, wheelchair-demonstration mid-training, and personalization from user interventions.
evidence.evidence_quote: ChairNav first pre-trains on large-scale cross-embodiment datasets transformed into the wheelchair domain, followed by mid-training on a small number of wheelchair demonstrations to eliminate remaining domain gaps. Finally, a post-training stage refines the deployed model from user interventions to personalize its behavior.

evidence.claim: The authors report that pre-training reduces lateral ADE by 18%, while post-training increases mean distance between user interventions from 29.2 m to 57.4 m.
evidence.evidence_quote: pre-training reduces lateral ADE by 18%, and post-training increases the mean distance between user interventions from 29.2 m to 57.4 m.

evidence.claim: On kilometer-scale urban sidewalk routes, the authors report autonomous operation for 93.4% of total driving time.
evidence.evidence_quote: Further evaluation on kilometer-scale urban sidewalk routes shows that our system operates autonomously for 93.4% of total driving time

topic_matches.title: HAVANA: A Hierarchical Video-Action Model for Vision-Language Navigation
topic_matches.overview: The authors introduce HAVANA, separating a slow language-conditioned latent planner from a fast local trajectory generator, without generating future video at inference. The authors report state-of-the-art performance over prior baselines on OmniNavBench and real-world generalization to unseen environments across robot embodiments.

evidence.claim: The authors introduce HAVANA, separating a slow language-conditioned latent planner from a fast local trajectory generator, without generating future video at inference.
evidence.evidence_quote: A slow system produces a compact language-conditioned latent plan from observation history, while a fast system combines the latest plan with the current observation to generate local trajectories. Their asynchronous execution enables rapid adaptation without repeated future prediction, and no future video is generated during inference.

evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance over prior baselines on OmniNavBench and real-world generalization to unseen environments across robot embodiments.
evidence.evidence_quote: Experiments on OmniNavBench demonstrate state-of-the-art navigation performance over prior baselines, while real-world deployments further show robust generalization to unseen environments across different robot embodiments.

topic_matches.title: Rollbot 2: Agile Locomotion by a Single-Actuator Spherical Robot
topic_matches.overview: The authors present a single-actuator spherical robot with redesigned mass distribution and onboard inertial and ultra-wideband sensing for learned steering and navigation. The authors report autonomous UWB-beacon approaches without motion capture and completion of a manually commanded indoor route. The authors report successful completion of all 16 waypoint-benchmark trials; the fastest traversal was over 70 times faster than the original Rollbot's run, with minor protocol differences.

evidence.claim: The authors present a single-actuator spherical robot with redesigned mass distribution and onboard inertial and ultra-wideband sensing for learned steering and navigation.
evidence.evidence_quote: Rollbot 2 preserves the single-actuator design while its redesigned mass distribution enables near-straight rolling and more direct travel toward commanded paths and beacon targets. Onboard inertial and ultra-wideband sensing support learned steering, beacon seeking, and waypoint following through one motor-velocity command.

evidence.claim: The authors report autonomous UWB-beacon approaches without motion capture and completion of a manually commanded indoor route.
evidence.evidence_quote: Rollbot 2 autonomously approaches UWB beacons without motion capture and completes a 468~m manually commanded indoor route at 0.87~m/s.

evidence.claim: The authors report successful completion of all 16 waypoint-benchmark trials; the fastest traversal was over 70 times faster than the original Rollbot's run, with minor protocol differences.
evidence.evidence_quote: On the shared 4.8~m ``N'' waypoint benchmark, all 16 trials complete the path with a mean traversal time of 10.8~s and mean time-averaged deviation of 7~cm. Its fastest traversal takes 8.0~s, over 70 times faster than the original Rollbot's 564~s run despite minor protocol differences.

topic_matches.title: Towards Reinforcement Learning for Space Robotics: Fast Training and Reliable Real-World Transfer
topic_matches.overview: The authors describe fast simulation-based reinforcement learning and report reliable transfer of learned policies to real hardware. The authors report reliable quadruped traversal of diverse real-world terrains, including a lunar-analog facility, after less than 20 minutes of training on a single consumer-grade GPU.

evidence.claim: The authors describe fast simulation-based reinforcement learning and report reliable transfer of learned policies to real hardware.
evidence.evidence_quote: This work demonstrates the use of a fast simulation-based training framework to learn control policies using reinforcement learning. The hardware requirements are minimal and the simulation-learned policies transfer reliably to the real world.

evidence.claim: The authors report reliable quadruped traversal of diverse real-world terrains, including a lunar-analog facility, after less than 20 minutes of training on a single consumer-grade GPU.
evidence.evidence_quote: a quadruped robot can learn to traverse diverse real-world terrains reliably---including in a lunar-analog facility---after less than 20 minutes of training on a single consumer-grade GPU.
